questions.question: Mr. Akai starts from Point A and drives 9 km towards west. He then takes a left turn, drives 9 km, turns left and drives 17 km. He then takes a left turn and drives 18 km. He takes a final left turn, drives 8 km and stops at Point P. How far (shortest distance) and towards which direction should he drive in order to reach Point A again? (All turns are 90-degree turns only, unless specified.)
questions.solution:
Given:

Mr. Akai starts from Point A and drives 9 km towards the west.

He then takes a left turn and drives 9 km.

He again takes a left turn and drives 17 km.

He then takes a left turn and drives 18 km.

Finally, he takes a left turn and drives 8 km and stops at Point P.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/eec4d0e0da686587f0802144bae5a64fbabbbdf126700fadeb5509e88c1d5a69.png] 

So, To reach Point A again, Mr. Akai must drive 9 km towards the south.

Hence, the correct answer is Option 1.

questions.question:
Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets.

(Note: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)

35 - 7 - 5

60 - 6 - 10
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Logic: First number = (Second number) × (Third number)

**35 - 7 - 5**

⇒ 7 × 5 = 35

**60 - 6 - 10**

⇒ 6 × 10 = 60

Now, checking the options:

Option 1) (81 - 7 - 8)

⇒ 7 × 8 = 56 (not 81)

Option 2) (40 - 5 - 9)

⇒ 5 × 9 = 45 (not 40)

**Option 3) (63 - 7 - 9)**

⇒ 7 × 9 = 63

Option 4) (12 - 4 - 2)

⇒ 4 × 2 = 8 (not 12)

Hence, the correct answer is **Option 3.**

Refer to the given number series and answer the question that follows. Counting to be done from left to right only. All numbers are single-digit numbers.

(Left) 7 5 2 4 9 5 3 8 9 1 2 6 6 6 8 4 5 3 9 1 7 9 8 6 3 6 9 (Right)

questions.solution:

Now,

We need to identify even numbers that are immediately preceded by an odd number and immediately followed by an even number.

So, the required condition is: **Odd Number – Even Number – Even Number**

(Left) 7, **__5, 2, 4__**, 9, 5, 3, 8, 9, __**1, 2, 6,**__ 6, 6, 8, 4, 5, 3, 9, 1, 7, **__9, 8, 6__**, 3, 6, 9 (Right)

Total even numbers satisfying the condition = 3

Hence, the correct answer is "**Option 3".**

questions.question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

Some bells are pots.

All pots are machines.

**Conclusions:**

(I): Some bells are machines.

(II): All machines are pots
questions.solution:
Given Statements:

Some bells are pots.

All pots are machines.

The least possible Venn diagram for the given statement is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9b3211ba16bfd95a18f544c8f352c0ea7398fa661d42a0f6f400ad9e7a15bc9a.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some bells are machines - **Follows **(Since some bells are pots and all pots are machines, those bells are also machines).

II. All machines are pots - **Does not follow** (All pots are machines does not mean all machines are pots).

So, only conclusion I follows.

Hence, the correct answer is **Option 1.**

questions.question: Aditi ranked 8 th from the top and 25 th from the bottom in her class. How many students are there in the class?
questions.solution:
Given:

Rank from top = 8

Rank from bottom = 25

Total number of students = (Rank from top + Rank from bottom) − 1

= (8 + 25) − 1

= 33 − 1

= 32

Here, there are **32 students** in the class.

Hence, the correct answer is** "Option 3".**

**Conclusions I:** All cats are mats

**Conclusions II:** Some cats are pots.

options.text: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows

Hence, the correct answer is** Option 3.**
